summary: The call wants interdisciplinary teams that build and test digital twins of bridges, buildings, or water systems, joining live sensing, physics or AI models, and decision support that operators will trust and use.

options.name: Bridge twin with trusted AI
options.angle: A sensing and modeling core on a real bridge testbed, with a human factors lead showing that operators trust the forecasts.

team.why: Runs bridge and historic building monitoring with model updating, the physical core of the twin.
team.evidence: Bayesian model updating of a masonry arch bridge from strain data (2025)

team.why: Builds physics-informed surrogates that make real-time prediction possible, and already publishes with Ava.
team.evidence: Physics-informed surrogates for real-time structural response (2025)

team.why: Brings the uncertainty quantification plan the call asks for.
team.evidence: Sequential UQ for digital twin calibration (2024)

team.why: Studies how emergency managers read uncertainty in AI forecasts, which answers the call's trust requirement.
team.evidence: How emergency managers read uncertainty in AI forecasts (2025)

gaps: A city or state DOT partner

email.subject: A team idea for Resilient Infrastructure Digital Twins
email.body:
Hi all,

We're writing because a new call lines up closely with your work and we think you'd make a strong team.

Ava leads bridge monitoring with model updating and could anchor the testbed.
Marcus builds physics-informed surrogates for real-time structural response.
Eli brings uncertainty quantification for twin calibration.
Theo studies how emergency managers read and trust AI forecasts.

The Resilient Infrastructure Digital Twins call is due March 15, 2027.

Let us know if we can help support you! We are happy to help you find more teammates, read a one-pager, and plan the proposal.

Best,
The Digital Twin Hub

options.name: Campus buildings as testbed
options.angle: Use campus buildings as a ready testbed, pairing an operational energy twin with fault detection and reduced-order models.

team.why: Already runs an operational twin of campus HVAC, which gives the project a working testbed from day one.
team.evidence: A campus-scale operational twin for HVAC fault detection (2025)

team.why: Makes the building models fast enough for real-time use and has published with Priya.
team.evidence: Reduced-order twins of a district heating network (2025)

team.why: Adds unsupervised anomaly detection on sensor streams.
team.evidence: Unsupervised anomaly detection in sensor streams (2024)

options.name: Community hazards and water
options.angle: A broader team focused on flooding and water systems, with community mapping and decision support for county emergency managers.

team.why: Builds spatial data pipelines for county emergency managers, the end users the call names.
team.evidence: Spatial data pipelines for county emergency managers (2024)

team.why: Forecasts soil moisture from in-field sensors, a base for a flood-side water twin.
team.evidence: Soil moisture forecasting from in-field sensors (2023)

team.why: Studies how emergency managers use AI forecasts, and has published with Rosa.
team.evidence: How emergency managers read uncertainty in AI forecasts (2025)

team.why: Adds time series machine learning for forecasting.
team.evidence: Unsupervised anomaly detection in sensor streams (2024)
